correctness.rationale: For A=2(u+1)v, B=(u+1)^2-2nv^2 and C=(u+1)^2+2nv^2, the exact identity \(C^2=2nA^2+B^2\) holds for every integer n. Direct substitution proves \(F_c=c^2 n^2 A^4\) and \(t^2=nxyzF_c\) when c is nonzero; the separate c=0 formula gives t^2=nxyzF_0. The factors u+1 and v do not divide B when n is nonzero, so A and B are coprime over Q[u,v]. Since C^2 has content one, the triple has gcd one in Z[u,v]. The included verifier checks the polynomial identities symbolically; the written argument proves the unrestricted claim.
